time_convention: t = frame / 24; frame = round(t * 24); frame 0 = t 0
units: pixels (x right, y down) and seconds; no metric scale assumed

camera.evidence: mean abs grey difference of the top 500 rows vs frame 0 <= 0.42 grey levels over all frames (noise only); no background shift
camera.view: side view of a walking robot in front of a hall wall; floor visible below y~818. Walk is parallel to the wall/image plane (apparent size constant), so one px scale applies

objects.name: robot
objects.description: the only moving object: grey cartoon robot (humanoid rig) with a large mushroom/dome-shaped grey head on a thin neck, egg-shaped torso with a large dark circular belly disk, ball-jointed arms with big hands, two legs with big flat feet
objects.motion: walks right-to-left (toward -x) the whole clip at a near-constant pace; ref point x goes 1612.3 (f0) -> ~1193.6 (f49): about -418 px in 49 frames (~8.5 px/frame, ~205 px/s); mask centroid x 1605.2 -> 1190.8 (-414 px). Vertical bob of the body ~ +-10 px
objects.reference_point: centre of the dark belly disk (rigid torso landmark nearest the pelvis; the true pelvis/hip origin is probably ~20-30 px lower, between the hip ball joints at y~885-895, but has no clean visual marker). For horizontal motion all reference choices agree within a few px

height_head_top_to_foot_bottom.note: max (~318-321) at mid-stance with legs together, frames 9-13 and 47-49; min (~297-301) at frames 23-28 (double support, legs spread)

length_along_walk_direction_bbox_x.note: varies with arm/leg swing; min ~121-125 at mid-stance (frames 8-9, 28-31, 46-49), max ~200-224 at frames 2-5, 18-24, 40-43
